rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: UKHSA's UK Malaria Expert Advisory Group updates malaria-prevention guidance for UK travellers each year.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: The 2026 guidance includes awareness of risk, bite prevention, chemoprophylaxis, country recommendations, diagnosis and special-risk groups.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Malaria-prevention advice should be tailored to the traveller and destination.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Mosquito-bite prevention remains important whether or not chemoprophylaxis is recommended.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Country recommendations support practitioners in giving specific advice for individual travellers.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Travellers should seek pre-travel health advice, ideally several weeks before departure when possible.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Chemoprophylaxis choice depends on destination risk, resistance patterns, medical history and contraindications.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Fever during or after travel to a malaria-risk area requires prompt clinical assessment with travel history disclosed.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: Malaria risk depends on destination, season, itinerary, accommodation, bite exposure, parasite resistance, prophylaxis adherence and traveller factors.

rows.source: UKHSA malaria prevention for travellers
rows.verified: UKHSA malaria evidence is destination-, traveller-, itinerary-, prophylaxis-, exposure- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: Chikungunya is predominantly transmitted to humans through bites from infected Aedes mosquitoes.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: Common symptoms include sudden fever and severe joint pain.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: Chikungunya can be clinically confused with dengue and other arboviral infections.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance emphasises mosquito-bite prevention for travellers to affected areas.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: Bite-prevention measures include repellents, covering exposed skin and suitable sleeping protection.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: A returning traveller infected abroad does not directly transmit chikungunya to other people through ordinary contact.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: UKHSA's HAIRS assessment considers the risk chikungunya presents to the UK population.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: Vaccine use requires adherence to current contraindications and precautions following safety review.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: Chikungunya risk depends on destination, season, Aedes activity, local transmission, bite exposure, accommodation, immunity and traveller health.

rows.source: UKHSA chikungunya prevention and risk assessment
rows.verified: UKHSA chikungunya evidence is destination-, vector-, traveller-, vaccine-, exposure- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
